You can quickly peek at formulas in Summaries, verify answers to problems in Practicums. But you won't find any "homework answers pdf" or "math answers for grade 7". Our goal is to teach you to understand the material yourself, derive formulas, and solve problems, not to give ready-made answers!

A detailed and interesting narrative. Its goal is to convey the material to you in every way possible: through examples, different formulations, jokes, and so on. At this stage, you just immerse yourself and delve into the material. You don't need to learn anything by heart!

A brief excerpt of the most important points from the article: definitions, theorems, formulas, etc. This is what must firmly remain in your head after studying the material, what needs to be memorized!

Various problems that will teach you to correctly apply theory in practice. Try to solve everything, including all "sub-problems" (they get trickier the further you go)! If you couldn't solve a problem and looked at the solution -- definitely solve it again immediately and then again the next day! There are more tips,
Practice is a mandatory part of learning! Never ever skip it. Without problem solving
you have red will vanish from your head in a matter of days. If you don't want to solve problems, then you don't want to learn math. Drop it and save your time for something else.
If the problem allows to generate "similar" variants, solve at least three of them. If you made a mistake, solve one more.

So you (think you have) solved the problem. Follow the chain of buttons under the problem, from left to right: "Check" → "Hint" → "Answer" → "Solution". Do not rush to open, for example, "Answer" immediately. First, try to pass the "Check" a couple of times, use "Hints"!
Even if you solved the problem correctly yourself, study its "Solution" regardless. It is important not only to get the correct answer, but also to understand the
Be sure to read "Notes" to problems! They contain important conclusions, generalizations, or interesting facts.
If you cannot repeat the solution of a problem without peeking into the solution -- you have not mastered the material.
Repeat until you solve it yourself!
Problem difficulty levels / Material knowledge levels:
= most elementary ideas about the material: plug a number into a formula.
= normal level of understanding and ability to operate with the material: transform formulas, combine them, solve problems in several steps.
level (not for everyone) = ability to apply material creatively and non-standardly + olympiad problems.

Don't even try to learn whole big topics in one day! It's counterproductive. It is better to spend a day on theory, summary, and "Elementary" level problems. And then another day/two on "Intermediate" level (you can even swing at "Advanced", it's cool there). At the same time, start every day by repeating key points from the summary.
